brief: Post-war steel Quonset: a semicircular arch of corrugated galvanized sheets painted silver-white, about 40 ft wide and 70 ft long, with a flat framed end wall holding a man door and a strip of small red-sashed windows, more windows let into the curved side. The example sits in a small North Dakota town; here it is the wheat farm's machine and grain-truck shed, with white propane tanks lying in the grass beside it.
